html:
Dujiangyan is an ancient irrigation and flood control system on the Min River in Sichuan, built around 256 BCE by the state of Qin. It still waters the Chengdu Plain today.

It was designed by Li Bing, the Qin governor of the conquered land of Shu. The Min River came down from the mountains and often flooded the plain. Instead of a dam, Li Bing used the river's own shape:

  • A levee shaped like a fish's mouth splits the river into an inner channel for irrigation and an outer channel for floods.
  • A spillway throws excess water and sand back into the outer river.
  • A channel cut through a hill, the Bottle Neck, controls how much water enters the plain.

The result turned Sichuan into a rich farming land, the "Land of Abundance", which fed the Qin armies and helped Qin unify China in 221 BCE. The system survived over two thousand years and was damaged but kept working after the Sichuan earthquake of 2008. Qin also built the Lingqu Canal in the south.
sum: Dujiangyan is an ancient irrigation and flood control system on the Min River in Sichuan, built around 256 BCE by the state of Qin. It still waters the Chengdu Plain today.
